html:
The Dhofar Rebellion was a war in the southern province of Oman from 1965 to 1976, between the sultan's government and rebels of Dhofar.

It began as a revolt against neglect by Sultan Said bin Taimur, who kept Oman closed and poor. After the British left Aden in 1967, the rebels turned Marxist and were armed by South Yemen, China and the Soviet Union. They held most of the Dhofar mountains.

The tide turned after Qaboos overthrew his father in 1970. He offered pardons, roads and schools to the Dhofaris, while British officers and troops sent by the Shah of Iran fought the rebels. The war ended in 1976. It was one of the few Cold War insurgencies in which the rebels were beaten outright.
sum: The Dhofar Rebellion was a war in the southern province of Oman from 1965 to 1976, between the sultan's government and rebels of Dhofar.
